checks.summary:
Verdict: ready for the pull request. I found nothing blocking. Every decision in decisions.md (1 to 8) is built in full. Nothing from decisions_fix4.md, decisions_fix5.md or issue #16 was removed or weakened. Every claim in the four groups' implement and repair reports is in the merged HEAD.

What I ran, with no edits, commits or pushes:
- Read the whole 77452a3..HEAD diff, including the hand-merged WEBSOCKET.md steps 7 and 8, the QUIRKS.md subsections and the auto-merged gameStore.js.
- Targeted backend tests on a throwaway database fr6_final_t: test_00_startup, test_ws_marks, test_ws_rolls, test_ws_connect, test_ws_circle, test_circle_rest, test_rest_broadcasts, test_campaigns and test_surface gave 662 passed and 1 failed. The failure was test_cors_allows_configured_origin_only, only because my environment did not set CORS_ORIGINS. Re-run with CORS_ORIGINS set on a fresh database fr6_final_t2, test_00_startup gave 36 passed, which covers the fresh path and both legacy-upgrade paths for activity_lines, held_mark and taken_mark_ids. Both databases are dropped.
- npx vite build of the merged frontend (output in the scratchpad) succeeded. The worktree is clean.
- No added line has an em dash, and no file names an AI model. Every pinned test was flipped or kept, not deleted. The history tests kept their names and gained a client fixture. The restart-rule test is renamed and pointed to from QUIRKS.md:149. The openapi snapshot adds only held_marks. test_surface's use_post_roll_ability expectation is now [character_update, roll_outcome, activity_log].

Seams I checked in the code:
- Connect order matches WEBSOCKET.md steps 7 and 8. A player gets character_update, circle_update, the held or replayed roll_result, ability_mark_offer, open intercepts, then activity_history. The Lightkeeper gets circle_update, the felt replay, then activity_history. A client mark sent again is processed after these frames, and a mark the server already took (taken_mark_ids) is answered once with the sheet.
- At a death the held mark is dropped in the scar's own commit, and the desk gets mark_offer_closed with dropped and no offer_id (the store's old branch handles it). After that, DEAD_REFUSED refuses every answer from the dead investigator's socket.
- The compare-and-swap `_take_held` commits before the first await in mark_or_offer and _let_the_mark_land. The use branches take the mark before their own synchronous commit. Each socket loads the character fresh per message with no await before the handler, so taken_mark_ids is race-free within the process.
- Sign out (logout) clears drafts and heldMarks through NO_OFFERS. endSession, the password reset and an undone email change pass keepDrafts.
- The roster is fetched on reconnect only while the investigator is active. Retire makes living investigators unaffiliated, so a living sheet coming back 'retired' can only mean a rejoin, as the store's leaveReplacedDesk branch assumes.

Data:
- activity_lines is written once per line in its own session. The missing foreign key is justified: a key check would take FOR KEY SHARE, which conflicts with the handler's FOR UPDATE on the campaign row. A line that fails to write is logged and still sent. Each line is pruned to the campaign's last 500, and each connect reads at most 500 rows.
- The cost is about four synchronous round trips per log line on the event loop, the same pattern as the rest of the WebSocket handlers. That is acceptable at this scale.
- Campaigns are only ever soft-deleted (no hard delete exists), so the missing foreign key orphans nothing.

The group choices Robert may not expect are covered in the items list, with my view on each. The issues are two "should" items (a doc gap in AUTH.md, and a dead investigator's own Accept to flag for Robert) and nits.

Lines with no campaign stay in memory. init_db creates the table with checkfirst. test_the_log_survives_a_restart and test_a_campaign_keeps_its_last_lines pass.

The store's offerDropped closes only the named card and the marks that answer sent on their way. QUIRKS.md and FAQ.md say so.

issues.problem: AUTH.md lists each WebSocket action's and REST route's rules, and the edit_sheet row already says 'not for a dead investigator (409)'. issues.item: A dead investigator's own socket can still Accept a relationship
issues.problem: After the fourth scar, the dead player's desk still shows Accept on a living member's pending proposal, and the server records it from the dead investigator's socket. But decisions_fix4 says 'A dead sheet is a record', and Robert may not expect the dead to agree to new relationships.
issues.fix: Flag it in the PR as an open call, without blocking. If Robert wants the record strict, refuse respond from the dead investigator's own socket (add it to DEAD_REFUSED and refuse REST respond when the responder is dead) and hide Accept on the dead desk. Accepting a proposal the dead made in life could stay allowed.

issues.item: Replaced desk: frames after the retired sheet still run
issues.where: frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:914-925 (character_update retired branch) and the roll_result, ability_mark_offer and activity_history handlers
issues.problem: After a reload or reconnect on an investigator retired by a rejoin, the server sends the retired sheet, then the replayed roll_result, any held ability_mark_offer and activity_history on the same socket. leaveReplacedDesk sends the desk to HOME and clears character, but closes the socket only in setTimeout(0). The frames already queued are handled first, so the replayed roll_result writes the retired investigator back into the store's character (and lastRoll) on the hub. resendMarks may also have sent kept marks for the retired character (refused 403). Nothing on the hub reads these today, and the next connect clears them, so nothing visible goes wrong. I found this by reading the code and did not run it in a browser.
issues.fix: In leaveReplacedDesk, close the socket synchronously (or set a flag), and have the roll_result, ability_mark_offer and activity_history handlers ignore frames once the stage is no longer DESK for that character.

issues.item: A stored held mark follows a released or retired investigator
issues.problem: Release, Leave, campaign Retire and a rejoin's retire do not clear characters.held_mark. An offer open at that moment is resent when the investigator's desk next opens, possibly in another campaign, and its decline lands the old mark there. The in-memory version behaved the same until a restart. Now the mark survives restarts, so the window has no end.
issues.fix: Clear held_mark (with mark_offer_closed dropped if a socket is open) in release_from_campaign and where a rejoin retires investigators. Otherwise note it in QUIRKS.md as kept on purpose.

issues.item: sameRoll compares a field the roll has no longer
issues.where: frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:307 (sameRoll); docs/refactor/WEBSOCKET.md:20-22 and the roll_result row
issues.problem: sameRoll compares a.action === b.action, but the roll objects (engine.roll_dice's result) have no action field. That check is always undefined === undefined, so 'same roll' means 'same dice'. The docs say 'the same action and dice' and 'the same roller, action and dice'. A newer roll from another device with identical dice and a different action would be merged as the old one (its outcome taken, its action not).
issues.fix: Pass the payload's action (message.payload.action, and the stored lastRoll's action) into the comparison, or drop 'action' from the docs.

issues.item: WEBSOCKET.md section 5 does not list the Lightkeeper's felt replay
issues.where: docs/refactor/WEBSOCKET.md:264 (roll_result row); dice_thrown has no row
issues.problem: The roll_result row's 'Emitted by' names a player's connect only, not the Lightkeeper's socket getting her own last roll with replayed. dice_thrown has no row in the outgoing table at all, an older gap, and the table's heading says every type in it has a handler. The felt replay is documented only in connect step 7.
issues.fix: Add 'connect, the Lightkeeper's felt (her own roll, replayed; since 2026-10-13)' to the roll_result row, and add a dice_thrown row that names its connect replay to the GM socket.

issues.item: QUIRKS.md ui subsection is out of date after the ui repair
issues.problem: The #44 bullet says Heading, List and Quote 'put the caret at the end of the line'. The repaired code keeps the caret where it was, shifted by the mark's length, which lands after the mark on an empty line. The #20 bullet names endSession and the password reset as keeping drafts but not the undone email change, which FAQ.md and the gameStore comment do name.
issues.fix: Reword the #44 bullet to match MarkdownMarks.prefixLines, and add the undone email change to the #20 bullet.

issues.item: Offers open at the moment of deploying are dropped
issues.problem: A soak or Death Defy offer held in the old process's memory when this build deploys is gone. The desk's answer gets mark_offer_closed with dropped, and the mark the Lightkeeper dealt never lands. This is what decision 1 asks for, and Robert said nobody is playing, so it is a one-time effect.
issues.fix: Add one line to the PR's deploy notes. No code change.

issues.item: Two candles on the Circle pages

issues.fix: Optional: drop the heading's candle on both pages, or flag it for Robert in the PR.

All six items are fixed on HEAD (claude/loving-fermi-2giawj). For each one I first saw the bug on the control (77452a3), then saw it fixed on HEAD at 390x844, 820x1180 and 1366x768, on both desks where it applies. Nothing blocking turned up and nothing broke. There were no page errors on HEAD; the only console errors were the expected WebSocket handshake failures while the backend was down for a restart.

What I tried besides the issues' own steps:
- #17: a whisper sent to the Lightkeeper stays private after a restart (Fay never sees it). A second tab, and a line written after the restart, both come back.
- #18: the Lightkeeper opening her desk after a restart sees the held box. A double press on Take the mark sends one answer.

- #43 (mark reached the server, reply lost): I dropped the server's replies, restarted the server and reloaded. The mark was sent again with the same mark_id and taken once (the server's stored taken_mark_ids caught the repeat).

Scripts are in /tmp/bc6_log_rolls (lib.js, setup.js, log17.js, c18.js, c23.js, c43.js, rolls.js, neigh.js, tab2.js). I checked all six items in Chromium at 390x844, 820x1180 and 1366x768. Each one was first seen failing on the control (77452a3, ports 8022/4022) and then working on HEAD (ports 8021/4021). I also checked the REST and WebSocket paths over the API on both servers. All six items are fixed on HEAD, and I found no blocking problem.

- #38: the control stores a fifth scar from the dead, and stores proposals and counters to and from the dead on REST and WebSocket.
